answer: Like a flat deposit, the witch tax makes every new identity pay 80 units up front, never refunded. The tax sits in escrow for 4 epochs; each honest epoch returns 12 units against fees, so a real user recovers the cost, while a fake caught cheating forfeits the rest and is frozen for 8 epochs. The summit of the cost curve is where forgery stops paying: 1,000 identities cost 80,000 units up front, and at a 30% detection rate 24,000 units burn. Rented reputation fails: the anchor deposit sticks to the identity, and the forge of new accounts cannot recycle the same capital.
